title: Bostic's virtuosity and the Bird story from Lockjaw Davis
summary: Tate describes Bostic's real style; Davis's story of Bostic out-playing Charlie Parker at a Bronx club.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Bostic must have been pretty young, too.

He was young, yeah, he was around my age. He was aroung -- yeah, he and I about the same age. But boy, he was a virtuoso on that horn, man, I mean -- and actually, what he made it big on wasn't really his style. He was in Bird vein, he played like Bird. But a lot of people didn't know that and you know, he just played like 'Flamingo'-type things and that's what they wanted to hear and that's where he made his gold. Lockjaw * told me about a -- he tells me -- well, Lockjaw was hip to him. You think you --
Okay. I got to tell you this.
Now, if I get nasty in here, you take that out, you know, because sometime I --
Well, this just goes into their archive. No one's going to hear this or see this besides (inaudible).

Lockjaw said one night, he and Bostick were playing a club up in the Bronx, the 8:45 Club. Well, I'm hip to him, I know how much he played. I been knowing all the time how much he played and he said Bird came in, brought his horn and he's got his name now, he's big. So he come in because Bostic was playing like the Bird style. He hadn't made the records and things like that, so Bird said, 'Let me go up and straighten this cat out and let him know who the boss is, you know?' He said Bird got his horn, boy, and Bostick started triple-tongueing on that -- he could triple-tongue. Started triple-tongueing and playing octaves and things and Jaws said, 'Buddy, he ran Bird crazy.' He says -- and Bird says -- he got off the stand, put his horn up and said -- he said, 'I really felt sorry for him because so many people saw him get his ass cut, you know, like from Bostick.' And play-
ing his thing, you know. And says, -- Lockjaw says, "I didn't have but $2.00, so I just went over to him, says, 'Come on, you can have all this because you need it worse than I do.'"
Said, "I gave him my last $2.00" He said, "Let me buy you a drink, man, because I know how you feel."

I said, "Man, I didn't know you was hip to him." He says, "Who?" He says, "I don't know anybody else." I says, "Well, man, I hired him." I says, "You know I know." I says, "I've known since 1930 how" -- he's really a virtuoso on that horn, you know." He could do anything. So we had him in that band, in the Holder band, and Claude Williams was in that band. It was a good band, but we never recorded and it was really a shame.
